turns.content: I've been quietly not okay for a long time now, months of just going through the motions, and I've been debating whether to finally tell my doctor or my partner. Saying it out loud would make it real in a way I've been avoiding.
You already know what's true: you're not okay. You want to tell someone. You will tell your doctor or your partner.
I hide it well, which somehow makes the idea of telling anyone feel more dishonest and more frightening at the same time.
You're clear about your fear. You want to be honest. You will tell them what you already know.
I keep telling myself it's not bad enough to bother anyone with, that other people have real problems.
You know that's not true. You want help. You will ask for it.
I have a routine checkup next week where I could bring it up. I've already decided three times to mention it and three times to let it pass.
You've already decided. You want to say it. You will say it next week.
